title: UTF-16 BOM round-trip is only detection-tested, not read/write-tested

evidence.quote: UTF-8/UTF-16 BOM detection on read and re-emission on write.

reasoning: The suite claims UTF-16 BOM preservation through read and write, but the UTF-16 tests stop at `detectBOM`. The document load and output-byte assertions only use a UTF-8 BOM, so a regression that detects UTF-16 but cannot parse it or re-emits the wrong encoding would not be caught.
recommendation: Add UTF-16LE and UTF-16BE file-based tests that load an actual encoded INI document, verify parsed keys, write it back, and assert both BOM bytes and decoded content.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Existing UTF-16 cases call the low-level detector only; they never construct `AWSConfigINIDocument(contentsOf:)` from UTF-16 data or assert write output for UTF-16.
suggestedRegressionTest: Create `[default]\nregion = us-east-1\n` encoded as UTF-16LE with `FF FE` and UTF-16BE with `FE FF`, load each via `AWSConfigINIDocument(contentsOf:)`, assert `bomKind`, assert the `region` key, write, then verify the output starts with the same BOM and decodes correctly as the same UTF-16 flavor.
minimumFixScope: Extend `BOMTests.swift` with file-level UTF-16LE and UTF-16BE round-trip tests.
